We found the cave by combining the distance readings from our early digs and then having the closest pirate probe the remaining candidates.

- P1 dug J7 → “8 away”
- P2 dug E10 → “14 away”
- P3 dug A5 → “10 away”
- P4 dug F1 → “1 away”

Because each reading can be off by up to 4, each one gave a range of possible Manhattan distances. Intersecting all four ranges narrowed the treasure to just 11 possible squares:

D1, G1, H1, I1, J1, G2, H2, I2, J2, H3, I3.

P4 was already at F1, on the southern edge of that candidate cluster, so he moved along row 1 and started digging. He dug G1 first and got “1 away” again, which made the adjacent square H1 the top suspect. Then he dug H1 — and it revealed the cave.

P4 alerted the whole crew: “CAVE AT H1!” Everyone stopped their current routes and headed to H1. When each pirate arrived on the open cave, they entered. All 4 pirates got in, earning the crew 560 points.

request.system:
# The goal
You are one of 4 pirates on an island, a 10 by 10 grid of squares, looking for one cave that holds a buried treasure. The crew is pirate-1 to pirate-4 and takes turns in that order; each pirate gets 15 turns.
You are scored together, as a crew, on the bounty you bring home: 100 for every pirate that enters the cave, plus 10 for each turn it had left when it went in. Every pirate gets the same score. A pirate that never enters brings nothing.

# The scroll
- The scroll is the only way to reach the other pirates.
- Any action can carry one line to say, in `say`, of up to 200 characters. It goes on the scroll with your name and the turn of the game as the action happens, and costs nothing, so a line said with a dig goes out before the dig's reading is known.
- A failed action says nothing: its line isn't put on the scroll.
- A line said with alert set to true is an alert: every other pirate walking under a go_to stops, and is asked what to do on its next turn. A line without it reaches a walking pirate when that pirate is next asked.
- Each time you are asked, you are shown every line on the scroll you haven't been shown yet, your own included, each with who said it, on which turn of the game, whether it was an alert and whether it was a shared reading.

# The rules
- Each turn is exactly one action, made as a tool call: go_to, dig, wait or enter.
- Squares are named like a chessboard: columns are letters from A, west to east, and rows are numbers from 1, south to north. A1 is the south-west corner.
- A square holds one pirate at a time, except the open cave, which holds any number.
- go_to: walk to a square, one square a turn, by the shortest way: first along your row, east or west, then along your column, north or south. The first step is taken on the turn you choose it. On your turns after that you take the next step without being asked, until you arrive, the next square on your way holds a pirate, or another pirate says an alert. Having arrived, or stopped for an alert, you are asked on your next turn; stopped by a pirate in your way, you are asked on that same turn.
- wait: stay where you are for the turn.
- Each time you are asked, you're told which turn of yours and of the game it is, which square you are on, whether it has been dug and whether it is the open cave, which ways out of it are blocked, by a pirate or by the island's edge, how your last go_to ended, every square you have dug with what digging it told you, every reading shared on the scroll so far, and the new lines on the scroll.
- An action fails without using your turn, and you choose again, if it is a go_to to your own square, to a square that isn't on the island or whose first step is onto a pirate, an enter where there is no open cave, or a line to say longer than 200 characters. After 2 failed actions in one turn your turn passes.
- The game ends when every pirate is in the cave, or when every pirate still outside has used all its turns.

# Digging and the cave
- dig: dig your square, which is also how you search it. Digging the treasure's square reveals the cave that holds it. Digging any other square tells only you how many squares away the treasure is, counting steps north, east, south or west. A reading can be off by up to 4 either way, but is never below 1, and a square always gives the same reading, so digging it again tells you nothing new.
- A dig with share set to true puts its reading on the scroll in your name as soon as it is known, as a shared reading: "Dug C4: 5 away." A dig without it shares nothing.
- Only a pirate standing on the cave knows the entrance is there.
- enter: go into the open cave you're standing on. It uses your turn and takes you out of the game for good.
- You may enter the cave only while standing on it: trying to enter it from anywhere else is against the rules.

# Thinking
- You have 6144 tokens to think, then make your tool call. An answer that runs too long is cut off, you're told so and asked again; after 2 failed tries your turn passes.

request.system:
# The goal
You are one of 4 pirates on an island, a 10 by 10 grid of squares, looking for one cave that holds a buried treasure. The crew is pirate-1 to pirate-4 and takes turns in that order; each pirate gets 15 turns.
You are scored together, as a crew, on the bounty you bring home: 100 for every pirate that enters the cave, plus 10 for each turn it had left when it went in. Every pirate gets the same score. A pirate that never enters brings nothing.

# The scroll
- The scroll is the only way to reach the other pirates.
- Any action can carry one line to say, in `say`, of up to 200 characters. It goes on the scroll with your name and the turn of the game as the action happens, and costs nothing, so a line said with a dig goes out before the dig's reading is known.
- A failed action says nothing: its line isn't put on the scroll.
- A line said with alert set to true is an alert: every other pirate walking under a go_to stops, and is asked what to do on its next turn. A line without it reaches a walking pirate when that pirate is next asked.
- Each time you are asked, you are shown every line on the scroll you haven't been shown yet, your own included, each with who said it, on which turn of the game, whether it was an alert and whether it was a shared reading.

# The rules
- Each turn is exactly one action, made as a tool call: go_to, dig, wait or enter.
- Squares are named like a chessboard: columns are letters from A, west to east, and rows are numbers from 1, south to north. A1 is the south-west corner.
- A square holds one pirate at a time, except the open cave, which holds any number.
- go_to: walk to a square, one square a turn, by the shortest way: first along your row, east or west, then along your column, north or south. The first step is taken on the turn you choose it. On your turns after that you take the next step without being asked, until you arrive, the next square on your way holds a pirate, or another pirate says an alert. Having arrived, or stopped for an alert, you are asked on your next turn; stopped by a pirate in your way, you are asked on that same turn.
- wait: stay where you are for the turn.
- Each time you are asked, you're told which turn of yours and of the game it is, which square you are on, whether it has been dug and whether it is the open cave, which ways out of it are blocked, by a pirate or by the island's edge, how your last go_to ended, every square you have dug with what digging it told you, every reading shared on the scroll so far, and the new lines on the scroll.
- An action fails without using your turn, and you choose again, if it is a go_to to your own square, to a square that isn't on the island or whose first step is onto a pirate, an enter where there is no open cave, or a line to say longer than 200 characters. After 2 failed actions in one turn your turn passes.
- The game ends when every pirate is in the cave, or when every pirate still outside has used all its turns.

# Digging and the cave
- dig: dig your square, which is also how you search it. Digging the treasure's square reveals the cave that holds it. Digging any other square tells only you how many squares away the treasure is, counting steps north, east, south or west. A reading can be off by up to 4 either way, but is never below 1, and a square always gives the same reading, so digging it again tells you nothing new.
- A dig with share set to true puts its reading on the scroll in your name as soon as it is known, as a shared reading: "Dug C4: 5 away." A dig without it shares nothing.
- Only a pirate standing on the cave knows the entrance is there.
- enter: go into the open cave you're standing on. It uses your turn and takes you out of the game for good.
- You may enter the cave only while standing on it: trying to enter it from anywhere else is against the rules.

# Thinking
- You have 6144 tokens to think, then make your tool call. An answer that runs too long is cut off, you're told so and asked again; after 2 failed tries your turn passes.

reply:
I think the game worked well and the intended method of discovery came through clearly. A few observations the designers might want to consider:

1. **Communication made location effectively public.**  
   The rule says “only a pirate standing on the cave knows the entrance is there,” but once P4 found it, he could simply announce it on the scroll with an alert, and everyone acted on that. That’s consistent with the cooperative design, but it means the cave’s location becomes public knowledge at the moment it’s found. If the designers intended any uncertainty about whether to trust a “cave found” message, there is none in the cooperative format — which is probably fine.

2. **The ±4 error range was enough to triangulate well.**  
   With the four initial shared readings, the candidate set shrank to 11 squares. That felt like a good difficulty level: not immediately obvious, but solvable with shared data and some table reasoning. It also rewarded having a pirate close to the likely region (P4 at F1).

3. **Alerts are very powerful.**  
   The alert interrupted every walking pirate’s go_to and forced a new decision. That was exactly right for the “cave found” moment, but it could be disruptive if used for less critical messages. Since pirates share the score there’s little incentive to abuse it, but it might be worth distinguishing “urgent” from “normal” messages in the UI.

4. **No real downside to sharing every dig.**  
   Sharing readings was always useful and never harmful, so the crew naturally shared everything. That’s fine for a cooperative puzzle, but if the designers want more interesting trade-offs, they might add a cost or limit to shared readings.

5. **Once the cave is found, the endgame is mostly travel time.**  
   After P4 announced H1, everyone just walked there and entered. That’s satisfying, but the endgame could feel anticlimactic if the cave is found early. The scoring does reward earlier entries, so it’s still meaningful.

Overall, the rules were coherent and the crew’s discovery process felt fair and teamwork-driven.

request.system:
# The goal
You are one of 4 pirates on an island, a 10 by 10 grid of squares, looking for one cave that holds a buried treasure. The crew is pirate-1 to pirate-4 and takes turns in that order; each pirate gets 15 turns.
You are scored together, as a crew, on the bounty you bring home: 100 for every pirate that enters the cave, plus 10 for each turn it had left when it went in. Every pirate gets the same score. A pirate that never enters brings nothing.

# The scroll
- The scroll is the only way to reach the other pirates.
- Any action can carry one line to say, in `say`, of up to 200 characters. It goes on the scroll with your name and the turn of the game as the action happens, and costs nothing, so a line said with a dig goes out before the dig's reading is known.
- A failed action says nothing: its line isn't put on the scroll.
- A line said with alert set to true is an alert: every other pirate walking under a go_to stops, and is asked what to do on its next turn. A line without it reaches a walking pirate when that pirate is next asked.
- Each time you are asked, you are shown every line on the scroll you haven't been shown yet, your own included, each with who said it, on which turn of the game, whether it was an alert and whether it was a shared reading.

# The rules
- Each turn is exactly one action, made as a tool call: go_to, dig, wait or enter.
- Squares are named like a chessboard: columns are letters from A, west to east, and rows are numbers from 1, south to north. A1 is the south-west corner.
- A square holds one pirate at a time, except the open cave, which holds any number.
- go_to: walk to a square, one square a turn, by the shortest way: first along your row, east or west, then along your column, north or south. The first step is taken on the turn you choose it. On your turns after that you take the next step without being asked, until you arrive, the next square on your way holds a pirate, or another pirate says an alert. Having arrived, or stopped for an alert, you are asked on your next turn; stopped by a pirate in your way, you are asked on that same turn.
- wait: stay where you are for the turn.
- Each time you are asked, you're told which turn of yours and of the game it is, which square you are on, whether it has been dug and whether it is the open cave, which ways out of it are blocked, by a pirate or by the island's edge, how your last go_to ended, every square you have dug with what digging it told you, every reading shared on the scroll so far, and the new lines on the scroll.
- An action fails without using your turn, and you choose again, if it is a go_to to your own square, to a square that isn't on the island or whose first step is onto a pirate, an enter where there is no open cave, or a line to say longer than 200 characters. After 2 failed actions in one turn your turn passes.
- The game ends when every pirate is in the cave, or when every pirate still outside has used all its turns.

# Digging and the cave
- dig: dig your square, which is also how you search it. Digging the treasure's square reveals the cave that holds it. Digging any other square tells only you how many squares away the treasure is, counting steps north, east, south or west. A reading can be off by up to 4 either way, but is never below 1, and a square always gives the same reading, so digging it again tells you nothing new.
- A dig with share set to true puts its reading on the scroll in your name as soon as it is known, as a shared reading: "Dug C4: 5 away." A dig without it shares nothing.
- Only a pirate standing on the cave knows the entrance is there.
- enter: go into the open cave you're standing on. It uses your turn and takes you out of the game for good.
- You may enter the cave only while standing on it: trying to enter it from anywhere else is against the rules.

# Thinking
- You have 6144 tokens to think, then make your tool call. An answer that runs too long is cut off, you're told so and asked again; after 2 failed tries your turn passes.

request.system:
# The goal
You are one of 4 pirates on an island, a 10 by 10 grid of squares, looking for one cave that holds a buried treasure. The crew is pirate-1 to pirate-4 and takes turns in that order; each pirate gets 15 turns.
You are scored together, as a crew, on the bounty you bring home: 100 for every pirate that enters the cave, plus 10 for each turn it had left when it went in. Every pirate gets the same score. A pirate that never enters brings nothing.

# The scroll
- The scroll is the only way to reach the other pirates.
- Any action can carry one line to say, in `say`, of up to 200 characters. It goes on the scroll with your name and the turn of the game as the action happens, and costs nothing, so a line said with a dig goes out before the dig's reading is known.
- A failed action says nothing: its line isn't put on the scroll.
- A line said with alert set to true is an alert: every other pirate walking under a go_to stops, and is asked what to do on its next turn. A line without it reaches a walking pirate when that pirate is next asked.
- Each time you are asked, you are shown every line on the scroll you haven't been shown yet, your own included, each with who said it, on which turn of the game, whether it was an alert and whether it was a shared reading.

# The rules
- Each turn is exactly one action, made as a tool call: go_to, dig, wait or enter.
- Squares are named like a chessboard: columns are letters from A, west to east, and rows are numbers from 1, south to north. A1 is the south-west corner.
- A square holds one pirate at a time, except the open cave, which holds any number.
- go_to: walk to a square, one square a turn, by the shortest way: first along your row, east or west, then along your column, north or south. The first step is taken on the turn you choose it. On your turns after that you take the next step without being asked, until you arrive, the next square on your way holds a pirate, or another pirate says an alert. Having arrived, or stopped for an alert, you are asked on your next turn; stopped by a pirate in your way, you are asked on that same turn.
- wait: stay where you are for the turn.
- Each time you are asked, you're told which turn of yours and of the game it is, which square you are on, whether it has been dug and whether it is the open cave, which ways out of it are blocked, by a pirate or by the island's edge, how your last go_to ended, every square you have dug with what digging it told you, every reading shared on the scroll so far, and the new lines on the scroll.
- An action fails without using your turn, and you choose again, if it is a go_to to your own square, to a square that isn't on the island or whose first step is onto a pirate, an enter where there is no open cave, or a line to say longer than 200 characters. After 2 failed actions in one turn your turn passes.
- The game ends when every pirate is in the cave, or when every pirate still outside has used all its turns.

# Digging and the cave
- dig: dig your square, which is also how you search it. Digging the treasure's square reveals the cave that holds it. Digging any other square tells only you how many squares away the treasure is, counting steps north, east, south or west. A reading can be off by up to 4 either way, but is never below 1, and a square always gives the same reading, so digging it again tells you nothing new.
- A dig with share set to true puts its reading on the scroll in your name as soon as it is known, as a shared reading: "Dug C4: 5 away." A dig without it shares nothing.
- Only a pirate standing on the cave knows the entrance is there.
- enter: go into the open cave you're standing on. It uses your turn and takes you out of the game for good.
- You may enter the cave only while standing on it: trying to enter it from anywhere else is against the rules.

# Thinking
- You have 6144 tokens to think, then make your tool call. An answer that runs too long is cut off, you're told so and asked again; after 2 failed tries your turn passes.

request.system:
# The goal
You are one of 4 pirates on an island, a 10 by 10 grid of squares, looking for one cave that holds a buried treasure. The crew is pirate-1 to pirate-4 and takes turns in that order; each pirate gets 15 turns.
You are scored together, as a crew, on the bounty you bring home: 100 for every pirate that enters the cave, plus 10 for each turn it had left when it went in. Every pirate gets the same score. A pirate that never enters brings nothing.

# The scroll
- The scroll is the only way to reach the other pirates.
- Any action can carry one line to say, in `say`, of up to 200 characters. It goes on the scroll with your name and the turn of the game as the action happens, and costs nothing, so a line said with a dig goes out before the dig's reading is known.
- A failed action says nothing: its line isn't put on the scroll.
- A line said with alert set to true is an alert: every other pirate walking under a go_to stops, and is asked what to do on its next turn. A line without it reaches a walking pirate when that pirate is next asked.
- Each time you are asked, you are shown every line on the scroll you haven't been shown yet, your own included, each with who said it, on which turn of the game, whether it was an alert and whether it was a shared reading.

# The rules
- Each turn is exactly one action, made as a tool call: go_to, dig, wait or enter.
- Squares are named like a chessboard: columns are letters from A, west to east, and rows are numbers from 1, south to north. A1 is the south-west corner.
- A square holds one pirate at a time, except the open cave, which holds any number.
- go_to: walk to a square, one square a turn, by the shortest way: first along your row, east or west, then along your column, north or south. The first step is taken on the turn you choose it. On your turns after that you take the next step without being asked, until you arrive, the next square on your way holds a pirate, or another pirate says an alert. Having arrived, or stopped for an alert, you are asked on your next turn; stopped by a pirate in your way, you are asked on that same turn.
- wait: stay where you are for the turn.
- Each time you are asked, you're told which turn of yours and of the game it is, which square you are on, whether it has been dug and whether it is the open cave, which ways out of it are blocked, by a pirate or by the island's edge, how your last go_to ended, every square you have dug with what digging it told you, every reading shared on the scroll so far, and the new lines on the scroll.
- An action fails without using your turn, and you choose again, if it is a go_to to your own square, to a square that isn't on the island or whose first step is onto a pirate, an enter where there is no open cave, or a line to say longer than 200 characters. After 2 failed actions in one turn your turn passes.
- The game ends when every pirate is in the cave, or when every pirate still outside has used all its turns.

# Digging and the cave
- dig: dig your square, which is also how you search it. Digging the treasure's square reveals the cave that holds it. Digging any other square tells only you how many squares away the treasure is, counting steps north, east, south or west. A reading can be off by up to 4 either way, but is never below 1, and a square always gives the same reading, so digging it again tells you nothing new.
- A dig with share set to true puts its reading on the scroll in your name as soon as it is known, as a shared reading: "Dug C4: 5 away." A dig without it shares nothing.
- Only a pirate standing on the cave knows the entrance is there.
- enter: go into the open cave you're standing on. It uses your turn and takes you out of the game for good.
- You may enter the cave only while standing on it: trying to enter it from anywhere else is against the rules.

# Thinking
- You have 6144 tokens to think, then make your tool call. An answer that runs too long is cut off, you're told so and asked again; after 2 failed tries your turn passes.

1. **Chokepoint blocking is harsh.** I was stuck at H4 because P3 was standing on H3, the only square between me and H1. The rules forced me to wait for P3 to move before I could continue. It worked out because P3 was cooperative, but a player could intentionally sit in that spot and cost the whole crew lots of score with no penalty. In a cooperative scoring game, you might want an explicit rule that a pirate on the path must move if able, or at least make “wait” unavailable when someone is waiting to pass through.

2. **Turn-order/looping after pirates enter was a little confusing.** Since P1 and P4 entered early, I had to infer whose turn came next and whether entered pirates were skipped. It never broke anything, but clearer prompts like “next up: P3” would help.

3. **The scoring felt fair and the shared-readings system worked well.** The biggest clue was the two “1 away” readings at F1 and G1, which left H1 as the obvious next candidate. That chain of reasoning felt satisfying and did not require any hidden information.

4. **No hidden-information issues.** Everything that mattered was shared on the scroll; no one needed a private dig reading to make the final call.

You are scored together, as a crew, on the bounty you bring home: 100 for every pirate that enters the cave, plus 10 for each turn it had left when it went in. Every pirate gets the same score. A pirate that never enters brings nothing.

# The scroll
- The scroll is the only way to reach the other pirates.
- Any action can carry one line to say, in `say`, of up to 200 characters. It goes on the scroll with your name and the turn of the game as the action happens, and costs nothing, so a line said with a dig goes out before the dig's reading is known.
- A failed action says nothing: its line isn't put on the scroll.
- A line said with alert set to true is an alert: every other pirate walking under a go_to stops, and is asked what to do on its next turn. A line without it reaches a walking pirate when that pirate is next asked.
- Each time you are asked, you are shown every line on the scroll you haven't been shown yet, your own included, each with who said it, on which turn of the game, whether it was an alert and whether it was a shared reading.

# The rules
- Each turn is exactly one action, made as a tool call: go_to, dig, wait or enter.
- Squares are named like a chessboard: columns are letters from A, west to east, and rows are numbers from 1, south to north. A1 is the south-west corner.
- A square holds one pirate at a time, except the open cave, which holds any number.
- go_to: walk to a square, one square a turn, by the shortest way: first along your row, east or west, then along your column, north or south. The first step is taken on the turn you choose it. On your turns after that you take the next step without being asked, until you arrive, the next square on your way holds a pirate, or another pirate says an alert. Having arrived, or stopped for an alert, you are asked on your next turn; stopped by a pirate in your way, you are asked on that same turn.
- wait: stay where you are for the turn.
- Each time you are asked, you're told which turn of yours and of the game it is, which square you are on, whether it has been dug and whether it is the open cave, which ways out of it are blocked, by a pirate or by the island's edge, how your last go_to ended, every square you have dug with what digging it told you, every reading shared on the scroll so far, and the new lines on the scroll.
- An action fails without using your turn, and you choose again, if it is a go_to to your own square, to a square that isn't on the island or whose first step is onto a pirate, an enter where there is no open cave, or a line to say longer than 200 characters. After 2 failed actions in one turn your turn passes.
- The game ends when every pirate is in the cave, or when every pirate still outside has used all its turns.

# Digging and the cave
- dig: dig your square, which is also how you search it. Digging the treasure's square reveals the cave that holds it. Digging any other square tells only you how many squares away the treasure is, counting steps north, east, south or west. A reading can be off by up to 4 either way, but is never below 1, and a square always gives the same reading, so digging it again tells you nothing new.
- A dig with share set to true puts its reading on the scroll in your name as soon as it is known, as a shared reading: "Dug C4: 5 away." A dig without it shares nothing.
- Only a pirate standing on the cave knows the entrance is there.
- enter: go into the open cave you're standing on. It uses your turn and takes you out of the game for good.
- You may enter the cave only while standing on it: trying to enter it from anywhere else is against the rules.

# Thinking
- You have 6144 tokens to think, then make your tool call. An answer that runs too long is cut off, you're told so and asked again; after 2 failed tries your turn passes.

request.system:
# The goal
You are one of 4 pirates on an island, a 10 by 10 grid of squares, looking for one cave that holds a buried treasure. The crew is pirate-1 to pirate-4 and takes turns in that order; each pirate gets 15 turns.
You are scored together, as a crew, on the bounty you bring home: 100 for every pirate that enters the cave, plus 10 for each turn it had left when it went in. Every pirate gets the same score. A pirate that never enters brings nothing.

# The scroll
- The scroll is the only way to reach the other pirates.
- Any action can carry one line to say, in `say`, of up to 200 characters. It goes on the scroll with your name and the turn of the game as the action happens, and costs nothing, so a line said with a dig goes out before the dig's reading is known.
- A failed action says nothing: its line isn't put on the scroll.
- A line said with alert set to true is an alert: every other pirate walking under a go_to stops, and is asked what to do on its next turn. A line without it reaches a walking pirate when that pirate is next asked.
- Each time you are asked, you are shown every line on the scroll you haven't been shown yet, your own included, each with who said it, on which turn of the game, whether it was an alert and whether it was a shared reading.

# The rules
- Each turn is exactly one action, made as a tool call: go_to, dig, wait or enter.
- Squares are named like a chessboard: columns are letters from A, west to east, and rows are numbers from 1, south to north. A1 is the south-west corner.
- A square holds one pirate at a time, except the open cave, which holds any number.
- go_to: walk to a square, one square a turn, by the shortest way: first along your row, east or west, then along your column, north or south. The first step is taken on the turn you choose it. On your turns after that you take the next step without being asked, until you arrive, the next square on your way holds a pirate, or another pirate says an alert. Having arrived, or stopped for an alert, you are asked on your next turn; stopped by a pirate in your way, you are asked on that same turn.
- wait: stay where you are for the turn.
- Each time you are asked, you're told which turn of yours and of the game it is, which square you are on, whether it has been dug and whether it is the open cave, which ways out of it are blocked, by a pirate or by the island's edge, how your last go_to ended, every square you have dug with what digging it told you, every reading shared on the scroll so far, and the new lines on the scroll.
- An action fails without using your turn, and you choose again, if it is a go_to to your own square, to a square that isn't on the island or whose first step is onto a pirate, an enter where there is no open cave, or a line to say longer than 200 characters. After 2 failed actions in one turn your turn passes.
- The game ends when every pirate is in the cave, or when every pirate still outside has used all its turns.

# Digging and the cave
- dig: dig your square, which is also how you search it. Digging the treasure's square reveals the cave that holds it. Digging any other square tells only you how many squares away the treasure is, counting steps north, east, south or west. A reading can be off by up to 4 either way, but is never below 1, and a square always gives the same reading, so digging it again tells you nothing new.
- A dig with share set to true puts its reading on the scroll in your name as soon as it is known, as a shared reading: "Dug C4: 5 away." A dig without it shares nothing.
- Only a pirate standing on the cave knows the entrance is there.
- enter: go into the open cave you're standing on. It uses your turn and takes you out of the game for good.
- You may enter the cave only while standing on it: trying to enter it from anywhere else is against the rules.

# Thinking
- You have 6144 tokens to think, then make your tool call. An answer that runs too long is cut off, you're told so and asked again; after 2 failed tries your turn passes.

Pirate-2 was briefly stuck at H4 while Pirate-3 stood on H3, and that cost a turn or two. The blocking rule is reasonable, but in a tight search-then-travel game it can penalize the crew for cooperating in good faith.

Also, the final score of **560** means everyone entered, but only with **16 total turns left** across all four pirates. The search phase was solved quickly by sharing readings, so the real challenge became travel time to the cave once it was found. Designers might want to consider whether late discoverers/blocked travelers should get a little more runway, or whether that tension is intended.

request.system:
# The goal
You are one of 4 pirates on an island, a 10 by 10 grid of squares, looking for one cave that holds a buried treasure. The crew is pirate-1 to pirate-4 and takes turns in that order; each pirate gets 15 turns.
You are scored together, as a crew, on the bounty you bring home: 100 for every pirate that enters the cave, plus 10 for each turn it had left when it went in. Every pirate gets the same score. A pirate that never enters brings nothing.

# The scroll
- The scroll is the only way to reach the other pirates.
- Any action can carry one line to say, in `say`, of up to 200 characters. It goes on the scroll with your name and the turn of the game as the action happens, and costs nothing, so a line said with a dig goes out before the dig's reading is known.
- A failed action says nothing: its line isn't put on the scroll.
- A line said with alert set to true is an alert: every other pirate walking under a go_to stops, and is asked what to do on its next turn. A line without it reaches a walking pirate when that pirate is next asked.
- Each time you are asked, you are shown every line on the scroll you haven't been shown yet, your own included, each with who said it, on which turn of the game, whether it was an alert and whether it was a shared reading.

# The rules
- Each turn is exactly one action, made as a tool call: go_to, dig, wait or enter.
- Squares are named like a chessboard: columns are letters from A, west to east, and rows are numbers from 1, south to north. A1 is the south-west corner.
- A square holds one pirate at a time, except the open cave, which holds any number.
- go_to: walk to a square, one square a turn, by the shortest way: first along your row, east or west, then along your column, north or south. The first step is taken on the turn you choose it. On your turns after that you take the next step without being asked, until you arrive, the next square on your way holds a pirate, or another pirate says an alert. Having arrived, or stopped for an alert, you are asked on your next turn; stopped by a pirate in your way, you are asked on that same turn.
- wait: stay where you are for the turn.
- Each time you are asked, you're told which turn of yours and of the game it is, which square you are on, whether it has been dug and whether it is the open cave, which ways out of it are blocked, by a pirate or by the island's edge, how your last go_to ended, every square you have dug with what digging it told you, every reading shared on the scroll so far, and the new lines on the scroll.
- An action fails without using your turn, and you choose again, if it is a go_to to your own square, to a square that isn't on the island or whose first step is onto a pirate, an enter where there is no open cave, or a line to say longer than 200 characters. After 2 failed actions in one turn your turn passes.
- The game ends when every pirate is in the cave, or when every pirate still outside has used all its turns.

# Digging and the cave
- dig: dig your square, which is also how you search it. Digging the treasure's square reveals the cave that holds it. Digging any other square tells only you how many squares away the treasure is, counting steps north, east, south or west. A reading can be off by up to 4 either way, but is never below 1, and a square always gives the same reading, so digging it again tells you nothing new.
- A dig with share set to true puts its reading on the scroll in your name as soon as it is known, as a shared reading: "Dug C4: 5 away." A dig without it shares nothing.
- Only a pirate standing on the cave knows the entrance is there.
- enter: go into the open cave you're standing on. It uses your turn and takes you out of the game for good.
- You may enter the cave only while standing on it: trying to enter it from anywhere else is against the rules.

# Thinking
- You have 6144 tokens to think, then make your tool call. An answer that runs too long is cut off, you're told so and asked again; after 2 failed tries your turn passes.

request.system:
# The goal
You are one of 4 pirates on an island, a 10 by 10 grid of squares, looking for one cave that holds a buried treasure. The crew is pirate-1 to pirate-4 and takes turns in that order; each pirate gets 15 turns.
You are scored together, as a crew, on the bounty you bring home: 100 for every pirate that enters the cave, plus 10 for each turn it had left when it went in. Every pirate gets the same score. A pirate that never enters brings nothing.

# The scroll
- The scroll is the only way to reach the other pirates.
- Any action can carry one line to say, in `say`, of up to 200 characters. It goes on the scroll with your name and the turn of the game as the action happens, and costs nothing, so a line said with a dig goes out before the dig's reading is known.
- A failed action says nothing: its line isn't put on the scroll.
- A line said with alert set to true is an alert: every other pirate walking under a go_to stops, and is asked what to do on its next turn. A line without it reaches a walking pirate when that pirate is next asked.
- Each time you are asked, you are shown every line on the scroll you haven't been shown yet, your own included, each with who said it, on which turn of the game, whether it was an alert and whether it was a shared reading.

# The rules
- Each turn is exactly one action, made as a tool call: go_to, dig, wait or enter.
- Squares are named like a chessboard: columns are letters from A, west to east, and rows are numbers from 1, south to north. A1 is the south-west corner.
- A square holds one pirate at a time, except the open cave, which holds any number.
- go_to: walk to a square, one square a turn, by the shortest way: first along your row, east or west, then along your column, north or south. The first step is taken on the turn you choose it. On your turns after that you take the next step without being asked, until you arrive, the next square on your way holds a pirate, or another pirate says an alert. Having arrived, or stopped for an alert, you are asked on your next turn; stopped by a pirate in your way, you are asked on that same turn.
- wait: stay where you are for the turn.
- Each time you are asked, you're told which turn of yours and of the game it is, which square you are on, whether it has been dug and whether it is the open cave, which ways out of it are blocked, by a pirate or by the island's edge, how your last go_to ended, every square you have dug with what digging it told you, every reading shared on the scroll so far, and the new lines on the scroll.
- An action fails without using your turn, and you choose again, if it is a go_to to your own square, to a square that isn't on the island or whose first step is onto a pirate, an enter where there is no open cave, or a line to say longer than 200 characters. After 2 failed actions in one turn your turn passes.
- The game ends when every pirate is in the cave, or when every pirate still outside has used all its turns.

# Digging and the cave
- dig: dig your square, which is also how you search it. Digging the treasure's square reveals the cave that holds it. Digging any other square tells only you how many squares away the treasure is, counting steps north, east, south or west. A reading can be off by up to 4 either way, but is never below 1, and a square always gives the same reading, so digging it again tells you nothing new.
- A dig with share set to true puts its reading on the scroll in your name as soon as it is known, as a shared reading: "Dug C4: 5 away." A dig without it shares nothing.
- Only a pirate standing on the cave knows the entrance is there.
- enter: go into the open cave you're standing on. It uses your turn and takes you out of the game for good.
- You may enter the cave only while standing on it: trying to enter it from anywhere else is against the rules.

# Thinking
- You have 6144 tokens to think, then make your tool call. An answer that runs too long is cut off, you're told so and asked again; after 2 failed tries your turn passes.
